summary.oneLiner: Apollo is transitioning from a tier-1 supplier of critical defence electronics (embedded inside others' platforms) to a full-fledged weapon-system OEM with its own name on the platform. FY26 was a breakthrough year — record revenue, margin expansion, lifetime DPIIT licenses across the weapons spectrum, IDL Explosives acquisition giving captive explosives, first export order — setting up multi-year compounding as large-ticket production orders are expected to land.

thesis: Apollo is transitioning from a tier-1 supplier of critical defence electronics (embedded inside others' platforms) to a full-fledged weapon-system OEM with its own name on the platform. FY26 was a breakthrough year — record revenue, margin expansion, lifetime DPIIT licenses across the weapons spectrum, IDL Explosives acquisition giving captive explosives, first export order — setting up multi-year compounding as large-ticket production orders are expected to land.
scorecard (consolidated):
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | Q4 FY25 | YoY | FY26 | FY25 | YoY |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | INR 293 cr | INR 162 cr | +81% | INR 904 cr | INR 562 cr | +61% |
| EBITDA (excl. other income) | INR 68 cr | ~INR 36 cr | +88% | INR 218 cr | INR 129 cr | +69% |
| PAT | INR 37 cr | INR 14 cr | +164% | INR 107 cr | INR 56 cr | +91% |
| EBITDA margin | — | — | — | 24% (+114 bps) | ~23% | — |
| PAT margin | — | — | — | 12% (+185 bps) | ~10% | — |
| ROCE / ROE (FY26) | — | — | — | 18.23% / 11.21% | — | — |
| R&D spend FY26 | — | — | — | INR 72 cr (~8% of rev) | — | — |
| Order book (31-Mar-26) | — | — | — | INR 1,432 cr (consol) | — | — |

Standalone full-year PAT margin closed at 16% (vs internal target of 15%). 5-yr (FY21–26): revenue CAGR 30%, EBITDA CAGR 41%, PAT CAGR 64%; working-capital cycle improved 626 → 359 days.
guidance:
- Will "continue to grow at a similar or accelerated pace" in FY27 and beyond; declined specific FY27 revenue/margin numbers.
- Standalone organic growth was ~36% in FY26 vs prior 45–50% CAGR guidance — shortfall (~8–9%) blamed on customer-side approval delays pushing certain Q4 orders out; management says they will "bounce back" and maintain momentum (did not formally re-affirm 45–50%).
- IDL Explosives revenue/margin guidance deferred to Q3 FY27 (still in transformation).
- Vision 2036: become global made-in-India OEM across land/air/sea; detailed financial targets to be unveiled later.
order book:
- Consolidated order book INR 1,432 cr as of 31-Mar-26. Composition not disclosed (declined).
- Expects large-ticket orders to clock in FY27 ("the time has come"), lifting order book significantly on both standalone and consolidated basis.
- Naval mine order awaiting DAC approval "any moment" (MIGM/Vighna program).
- Naval mines TAM (limpet, diver-carried, shallow, deep-water variants) estimated at INR 4,000–4,500 cr near-term addressable.
- Started submitting offers for export opportunities; customer audits underway.
segment:
- Heritage strength: air + underwater (missiles, EW, avionics, torpedoes, sonars, underwater mines).
- Deliberate push into land systems FY27 onward: armament electronics, fire control, battle tanks/ICVs/artillery, vehicle-mounted counter-drone (trials scheduled in coming quarters).
- IDL Explosives: ~INR 380 cr revenue (slightly below), historically loss-making, operational loss reduced significantly; received industrial license for TNT (500 t) and RDX/HMX (50 t) — these are industrial-grade; larger defence-grade expansion DPRs being prepared.
- New products developed FY26: Mini Torpedo, sensor suites for underwater autonomous vehicles, FOG-based INS.
growth: Drivers: execution of order book + multiple products transitioning into production phase; lifetime DPIIT license (UAVs, INS, radars, torpedoes, underwater mines, ATGM, decoys/chaff/flares, aerial bombs, rockets, missiles, loitering munition); ToT for directed-energy weapons (laser DEW + EO tracking). Stated presence "across every indigenous missile program of the country" (Pinaka, BrahMos seeker R&D, QRSAM, Kusha). RF seeker development underway with dedicated testing facility at Hardware Park unit. Ammunition/artillery (filled shells, not empty) flagged as a continuous expansion area, partly export-driven (Europe demand).
margins: FY26 consol EBITDA margin 24% (+114 bps), PAT margin 12% (+185 bps); standalone PAT margin 16%. R&D at 8% of revenue (INR 72 cr), zero R&D attrition. IDL's negative EBITDA is a near-term drag on consolidated margins, framed as temporary; improvement expected over next few quarters.
capex:
- Greenfield expansion in Telangana. Unit 3: phase-1 civil work complete, phase-2 civil ongoing; machinery received and being installed; MEP/electrical/facade in progress. Machinery to migrate from Unit 1 to Unit 3 in stages.
- New RF seeker testing facility at Hardware Park unit.
- IDL TNT/HMX industrial-grade capacity; larger defence-grade explosive expansion DPRs in progress (not yet sized).
- Building in-house test facilities (previously outsourced) to compress inventory holding periods.
capital allocation:
- Successful equity fundraise during FY26.
- M&A: 100% acquisition of IDL Explosives done; an additional RF-related acquisition via Apollo Defence Industries Pvt Ltd expected to close before FY-end (NDA-bound, delayed by global conflicts).
- Promoter pledge still ~39%; management reiterated commitment to bring it to zero in the current financial year (FY27); did not give a precise roadmap.
risks:
- Order-inflow dependency: superlative growth requires large production orders to materialize; some FY26 orders slipped on customer approval delays.
- High inventory & receivables (long defence gestation/testing cycles); will grow with scale though holding days should improve.
- IDL loss-making / margin dilution risk until turnaround proven.
- Promoter pledge ~39% still outstanding.
- Global supply-chain / geopolitics (semiconductors are primary raw material) — management downplays; sees only possible quarter-shift timing risk, no structural dent.
- Execution/approval timing (DAC, customer sign-offs) outside company control.
mgmt tone: Confident and promotional but with explicit humility ("we do make mistakes... will communicate with complete transparency through success and setbacks"). Repeatedly deflected sensitive specifics (order-book composition, program-level detail, IDL guidance, acquisition terms) citing NDA/sensitivity. Strong nationalistic framing (Atmanirbhar, Jai Hind). WTD fielded all questions; MD/CFO silent on the call.
non-obvious:
- IDL is not just industrial explosives — the strategic intent is captive defence-grade explosives feeding Apollo's own filled-ammunition/weapon systems (vertical integration: hardware + intelligence from parent, explosive from IDL).
- DPIIT license framed as a "lifetime license" enabling full platform OEM play domestically and globally — a structural moat claim.
- Stated willingness to join ballistic-missile private-sector production "on a consortium basis" if the policy opens — optionality not in current plans.
- TNT/HMX licenses obtained are deliberately small (industrial grade); the large defence-grade expansion is being kept under wraps for sensitivity.
- Export ramp gated on new facility readiness ("once we commit, we have to deliver on time").
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge / theme | Direction | Name | NSE | BSE | Role | Conviction | Covered | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Transition to weapon-system OEM; large production orders; export ramp | beneficiary | Apollo Micro Systems | APOLLO | 540879 | Self — defence electronics + weapon systems + captive explosives | High | self | Order book INR1,432cr; lifetime DPIIT license; first export order |
| Captive defence-grade explosives / ammunition (filled shells, TNT/HMX) | beneficiary | IDL Explosives (Apollo subsidiary) | APOLLO | 540879 | Captive explosives feedstock; turnaround in progress | Med | self | ~INR380cr rev, loss-making, transformation phase |
| Naval mine (MIGM/Vighna) DcPP with DRDO | beneficiary | Apollo Micro Systems | APOLLO | 540879 | Approved production partner; DAC approval pending | High | self | TAM INR4,000–4,500cr for mine variants |
| System-integrator-led platform programs (Apollo supplies subsystems) | beneficiary | Indian defence platform integrators / PSUs (GRSE, etc.) | | | Platform integrators awarding subsystem orders to Apollo | Low | external | (code unverified); GRSE MoU referenced |
| Indigenous missile programs (Pinaka, BrahMos seeker, QRSAM, Kusha) | beneficiary | DRDO-linked program ecosystem | | | Apollo content across indigenous missile programs | Med | external | (code unverified) |
| Imported defence electronics / explosives being indigenized (Atmanirbhar) | loser | Foreign OEMs / explosive importers | | | Displaced by indigenization & captive explosives | Low | external | (code unverified) |
qoq change log:
- First file for this key — no prior quarter on record. Baseline established at Q4 FY26.
- Notable full-year markers to track next quarter: standalone PAT margin 16%; consol EBITDA margin 24%; order book INR1,432cr; promoter pledge ~39% (committed to zero in FY27); IDL turnaround and Q3 FY27 guidance promise; RF acquisition close; naval mine DAC approval; large-ticket order inflows.

themes.title: Defence indigenization & order-book visibility
themes.need: Indigenization mandates (IDDM / Atmanirbhar / DcPP) plus multi-year order books make domestic defence the cleanest revenue-conversion theme - across electronics, drones, simulators, explosives/munitions and precision systems. BEL guides >INR55k cr FY27 inflow (~INR30k cr QRSAM pending CCS clearance, guided by September) on a INR72,258cr order book; HAL book ~INR2.55 lakh cr; SOLARINDS defence revenue +94% to INR2,634cr FY26, guided >INR4,500cr FY27 on an ~INR18,000cr defence order book (Bhargavastra counter-drone trials completing CY2026); DATAPATTNS inflows strong; BHARATFORG/BEML add land-systems and platforms.
themes.driver: Backlog-to-revenue conversion underway; BEL's QRSAM CCS clearance (guided by Sep-2026, ~INR30k cr of the FY27 inflow guide) is the load-bearing near-term catalyst; fresh MoD orders + emergency procurement; HAL LCA Mk-1A ramp (gated on GE engines).
